episodes.205347: A surface cold front stationed across west-central Pennsylvania produced scattered thunderstorms into central and eastern Pennsylvania during the afternoon and evening hours of September 4, 2025. Thunderstorms remained strong-to-severe across north-central Pennsylvania, producing isolated wind damage. Shear in the lowest levels allowed for a brief, weak tornado to form in Lancaster County.
episodes.205447: On the evening of September 4, a broken line of thunderstorms developed and produced gusty winds across western Minnesota. The strongest gust was 62 mph at the Granite Falls airport. ||As the storms moved east, the produced two weak tornadoes. These tornadoes caused mainly crop damage, but there was also some damage to a couple groves of trees, and some roof damage to a hog barn. The tornadoes were both rated EF0, with peak winds of 70 to 80 mph.
episodes.205613: A couple of strong thunderstorms produced gale-force wind gusts off the coast of Annapolis over the middle Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.205662: A cold front pushing through the Mid-South in an environment of 30 knots of effective shear and plenty of CAPE fueled several severe thunderstorms that tracked across portions of East Tennessee, producing several instances of severe wind damage and severe hail.
episodes.205663: A cold front pushed into the Mid-South in an environment with plenty of CAPE and effective shear of 30 knots. This caused a severe thunderstorm to move across the southern portions of southwest Virginia, yielding damaging winds.
episodes.205713: During the late evening hours of September 3rd, a storm in Bates County brought damaging wind gusts and some large hail.
episodes.205835: An intense supercell thunderstorm developed over portions of Saline County during the late afternoon hours of September 3rd. This storm weakened as a second supercell thunderstorm developed across portions of McPherson County. This storm moved across portions of McPherson, Harvey, and Sedgwick and produced several reports of large hail up to baseball size. A third supercell storm developed across southwest McPherson County and once again, tracked across Harvey and Sedgwick counties. Large hail up to baseball size and wind gusts in excess of 70 mph were reported. Extensive damage to roofs, trees, siding, and vehicles occurred across McPherson, Harvey, and Sedgwick counties.
episodes.205998: Heavy monsoon rains caused flash flooding in a couple of areas.
episodes.206266: Several supercells developed early evening on September 3 along a cold front, producing hail as large as two inches in diameter.
episodes.206619: A cold front approached northern New York, specifically the  St. Lawrence county region during the afternoon of September 4th into a marginally unstable airmass. A broken line of showers and thunderstorms moved across St. Lawrence county with two storms producing marginal severe weather in the form of storing wind gusts and downed trees.
episodes.206631: A cold front moving across the area triggered scattered showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening. With plenty of wind shear in place, the environment was favorable enough for a few storms embedded within a line to produce strong, damaging wind gusts across north-central New York. It was determined that an EF0 tornado had spun up near Ava in Northern Oneida County.
episodes.206998: As a front pushed into northern portions of the Quad State, a SW to NE oriented line of storms organized in Southern Illinois late evening and tracked through Southwest Indiana around midnight CST. A storm developed behind that line in Posey County which went on to blow down a hardwood tree onto a barn in southwestern Evansville. MLCAPE was around 250J/kg while effective bulk shear was 30kts.
episodes.206999: As a front pushed into northern portions of the Quad State, a SW to NE oriented line of storms organized in Southern Illinois late evening and tracked through Henderson and Daviess Counties around midnight CST. Wind gusts around 55 mph were reported five miles south of Stanley in Western Daviess County, while penny size hail was measured east of Owensboro. MLCAPE was around 250J/kg while effective bulk shear was 30kts.
episodes.207055: Scattered to numerous thunderstorms developed over the northern half of AZ as well as near the International Border during the afternoon hours with more isolated activity developing across the foothills and higher terrain areas east of Phoenix. All of this activity was due to strong upper-level ascent associated with a low pressure system along the west coast and another upper-level disturbance over northern Mexico. Outflow boundaries from the aforementioned activity sparked new thunderstorm activity during the evening hours across much of the south-central AZ lower deserts, including the Phoenix area. The combination of MLCAPE values between 500-1000 J/kg and DCAPE values of around 1500 J/kg supported strong to locally severe downburst wind gusts. PWATs were also near 1.5, supporting an environment conducive to high rainfall rates with these thunderstorms and thus some flooding impacts.
episodes.207173: A broken line of thunderstorms developed along a cold front which pushed across southwest Minnesota during the late afternoon and evening hours.  An appreciable sub-cloud dry layer led to marginally severe wind gusts with sporadic tree damage.
episodes.207298: During the afternoon hours of September 3rd, a storm brough a severe wind gust to Miami County.
episodes.207660: A line of showers and storms, associated with a cold front and lee trough, moved into central and southern Virginia in the late afternoon and evening hours of September 4. While weak instability generally limited storm intensity, the strongest storms produced isolated areas of wind damage. Storms weakened considerably as they approached the coast overnight.
episodes.207731: On September 4, a pre-frontal trough and cold front crossing the region caused severe thunderstorms to develop across the eastern half of the Buffalo forecast area. With 40+ knots of 0-6 km shear available and CAPE values of around 1,000 J/kg for areas east of the Genesee Valley. As showers along the trough and front encountered this more favorable area and thunderstorms developed and became severe with damaging wind gusts.
episodes.207834: A strong ridge over the region resulted in a heat risk through the middle of the week, and a return of monsoonal moisture allowed for thunderstorms the develop, mainly over the mountains and deserts throughout the rest of the week.
episodes.207838: Multiple clusters of thunderstorms developed and moved southeast ahead of a cold front across east Tennessee and western North Carolina throughout the evening. Several storms produced brief severe weather throughout western NC.
episodes.207858: A line of showers and storms, associated with a cold front and lee trough, moved into central and southern Virginia in the late afternoon and evening hours of September 4. While weak instability generally limited storm intensity, the strongest storms produced isolated areas of wind damage as well as lightning. An isolated lightning strike occurred in central Virginia.

A thunderstorm moved through far Northern Oneida County that had broad rotation tighten up as it approached Ava. A weak tornado touched down and traveled about 3 miles and was on the ground for approximately 8 minutes. The first area of damage that was surveyed was off of Vary Road west of Ava with a few trees down as well as scattered tree debris that fell in a convergent pattern. The next stop was in the town of Ava where there was damage that indicated a maximum of 80 mph winds. A chicken coop was lofted and set down several yards from its original location as well as a large tree that fell on a pig pen. Once again trees on the south side of the property fell in a convergent pattern. The last location that had any damage was at a farm house a |little over a mile to the east of Ava on Flint Town Road where a large, partly rotten tree fell on the house. Minor damage occurred to the property from the tree falling on it but no visible wind damage was seen. With the tree being weak and no other significant tree damage in the vicinity and no more visible damage to the east, this was determined to be roughly the end of the tornado's path.
